prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1298; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a report that the insured vehicle was struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and is handling the claim directly.

Entry 2: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed a left-turn collision and said the claimant's vehicle came across the oncoming lane. The other driver's account matches the scene description and is consistent with the damage reported so far.

Entry 3: Reviewed scene photos and two independent witness statements. Both witnesses describe the same sequence of events, and both place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact, as confirmed by the responding officer's report.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle. The front-quarter damage and the airbag deployment line up well with the reported impact angle and speed. A few older scratches along the lower rear panel may predate this loss and have been noted for the appraiser.

Entry 5: Claimant reports a knee injury that required urgent care and then a longer course of physical therapy than is typical for this type of injury. Medical records are being requested to confirm the treatment timeline and the diagnosis.

Entry 6: Claimant's medical history shows a minor strain in the same knee several years ago, which healed fully according to the prior provider's notes. The earlier episode does not appear to have required ongoing care, but it will be considered when evaluating the current treatment.

Entry 7: Claimant gave a follow-up statement adding a few small details about the moments before the collision, such as the traffic signal color and the speed of the approaching car. The core account has not changed from the first report.

Entry 8: A neighbor contacted the desk and stated the vehicle looked damaged a few weeks before the reported collision date. The statement is being noted and will be checked against photos, repair estimates and the policy's coverage history. The driver is named on the policy, and coverage is not in question at this stage.
